gloss: retainer fee; initial payment; upfront fee

definitions.gloss: retainer fee; upfront fee paid when work begins
definitions.explanation: A fee paid at the start of a job, especially to a lawyer or contractor, separate from the final reward or balance. It is typically charged regardless of the outcome.

examples.japanese: {着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}を{払|はら}う。
{弁護士|べんごし}に{着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}を{支払|しはら}った。
examples.english: I paid the lawyer a retainer fee.

examples.japanese: {着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}は{結果|けっか}に{関係|かんけい}なく{返|かえ}ってこないことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: The retainer is often non-refundable regardless of the outcome.

notes:
Common in legal fees and construction or design contracts, where it is paid before work starts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}を{請求|せいきゅう}する: to charge a retainer
- {着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}{無料|むりょう}: no upfront fee
- {着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}の{相場|そうば}: the going rate for a retainer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}: contingency fee — paid only on a successful result, after the work
- {手付金|てつけきん}: deposit — a down payment securing a sale or contract
